inputs.count_table_relationship: The tables are identifier-keyed count-equivalent but have different row order.

protocol.question: Does count-table row order change MAGeCK test statistics or downstream hit calls when every keyed guide, gene, and count is identical?
protocol.reference_command: mageck test -k escneg.count.txt -t ESC1 -c plasmid -n baseline/yusa
protocol.candidate_command: mageck test -k dotmatch-0.6.1.counts.tsv -t ESC1 -c plasmid -n candidate/yusa
protocol.comparison_command: python3 scripts/compare_mageck_test_results.py baseline/yusa.gene_summary.txt candidate/yusa.gene_summary.txt baseline/yusa.sgrna_summary.txt candidate/yusa.sgrna_summary.txt --fdr-threshold 0.05
protocol.success_criteria: Exact guide/gene membership, all sgRNA fields, all non-rank gene fields, and FDR hit sets; rank variation allowed only as a permutation within identical score/p-value/FDR tie blocks.
protocol.failure_criteria: Fail on abnormal or partial output, missing/extra identifiers, any sgRNA-field mismatch, any non-rank gene-statistic mismatch, rank movement across tie blocks, or a changed FDR hit set.

negative_result: MAGeCK 0.5.9.5 assigns ordinal gene ranks within exact score/p-value/FDR ties according to input-dependent order. A naive exact rank or top-N comparison can therefore report differences even when every count, sgRNA statistic, non-rank gene statistic, and FDR call agrees.
claim_boundary: This establishes downstream MAGeCK output equivalence for this single Yusa contrast under explicit tied-rank semantics. It does not establish that MAGeCK statistics, DotMatch counts, the screen design, or the resulting gene hits are biologically correct, and it is not external adoption evidence.
